title: Autonomous Low-Cost Ocean Observation Platform for Polar and Southern Oceans
department: National Centre for Polar andOcean Research (NCPOR)
description: Design and develop an indigenous, low-cost, autonomous ocean observation platform capable of long-term deployment in harsh polar and Southern Ocean environments for measuring key oceanographic and atmospheric parameters.
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on autonomous applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a hardware build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on moderate engineering scope. Sustainability (5/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (1/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 16/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Autonomous Low-Cost Ocean Observation Platform for Polar and Southern Oceans

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an affordable, self-sufficient ocean sensor buoy that can survive and keep measuring for a long time in the brutal Southern Ocean, where existing observation equipment is either too expensive or doesn't survive the conditions.
overview.why_it_matters: The Southern Ocean is critically undersampled because it's so hard to operate equipment there. A genuinely durable, low-cost platform would meaningfully expand our data coverage of this important, poorly-monitored region.
pain_points: Existing ocean observation platforms are often too expensive for large-scale deployment.
Harsh polar/Southern Ocean conditions cause high equipment failure rates.
Long-term autonomous operation in these extreme conditions remains a real engineering challenge.
overview.background: Polar and Southern Ocean regions are critically undersampled for oceanographic and atmospheric data, and existing observation platforms struggle with cost and durability in these harsh conditions. Verified against the official SIH26065 portal listing (Ministry of Earth Sciences / NCPOR) — the description above matches the official text; this is the full scope as published, not an inference gap.
overview.whats_being_asked: An indigenous, low-cost, autonomous ocean observation platform capable of long-term deployment measuring key oceanographic/atmospheric parameters in harsh polar and Southern Ocean environments.
expected_solution: Long-term durability suited to extreme polar/Southern Ocean conditions.
Measurement of key oceanographic and atmospheric parameters.
Data transmission capability from remote deployment.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate as scored, though genuine long-term survivability in these conditions is a much harder engineering challenge than the score reflects, similar to other MoES hardware PS in this batch.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low as scored, but real long-term durability validation in extreme ocean conditions requires testing timeframes and environments no hackathon can provide.

competitive_landscape.note: Specialized marine hardware engineering PS, requires both hardware building skill and oceanographic domain knowledge.

innovation.note: Genuine value in the low-cost, durability-focused design approach for an underserved observation region.

invention.tag: Low on paper, Genuinely Hard in reality
invention.note: Real long-term extreme-condition durability can't be validated in a 36-hour hackathon window.

technical_feasibility.tag: Workable for a Scaled Prototype, Not for Validated Long-Term Deployment
technical_feasibility.note: A basic sensor-buoy prototype demonstrating core measurement capability is achievable; genuine long-term extreme-condition survivability cannot be tested at a hackathon.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuinely expands observation coverage of a critically undersampled ocean region if actually deployed at scale.

architecture.note: Sensor package, power system, and data transmission integrated into one durable platform, real but manageable integration if scoped to a basic prototype.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Yellow. Build a basic sensor-buoy prototype demonstrating core measurement and data-transmission capability, and present the extreme-durability engineering as a design proposal grounded in research, being explicit that long-term validation is beyond hackathon scope.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: A basic version of this (sensor package, power, transmission) is genuinely buildable and testable in 36 hours, unlike the deep-ocean sensor PS nearby.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Claiming genuine long-term Southern Ocean durability without any real extreme-condition testing would be an overclaim, this needs honest scoping.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope to a working basic sensor-buoy prototype (measurement and data transmission working) plus a researched durability design proposal, not a claimed long-term-survival-validated system.

idea_0_4: Choose 2-3 key oceanographic/atmospheric parameters to measure (e.g. temperature, pressure, basic weather sensors) for your prototype.
Research real polar/Southern Ocean survivability requirements (extreme cold, wave action, biofouling, power constraints) for your durability design proposal.
Split: one person on the sensor/power/transmission prototype, one on the durability design research.
prototype_4_22: Build your basic sensor package with power system and data logging.
Build basic data transmission capability (even simulated satellite-uplink logic if real hardware isn't available).
Start your durability design proposal, housing material, sealing approach, cold-weather power management.
integration_22_30: Get your full sensor-to-transmission pipeline working end to end.
Test your sensor package's basic functionality under any available approximated harsh conditions (e.g. cold storage test for the electronics).
Compile your durability engineering proposal with real research grounding.
polish_30_36: Prepare your working prototype and your durability proposal as two distinct, honestly-labeled deliverables.
Rehearse explaining the low-cost design choices and how they compare to expensive existing platforms.
Prepare to discuss what real field-testing and long-term deployment would require.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your prototype actually collecting and transmitting real sensor data live, even a basic working measurement-and-transmission loop is concrete evidence, paired with a well-researched durability proposal for the extreme-condition engineering you couldn't fully validate.

strengths: Basic version genuinely buildable and testable within 36 hours.
Addresses a real, scientifically significant observation gap (undersampled Southern Ocean).
weaknesses: Genuine long-term extreme-condition durability can't be validated at hackathon scope.
Requires both hardware engineering and oceanographic domain knowledge together.

team_fit.approach: Build the working sensor-transmission core first, then invest remaining time in the durability design research and proposal.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Data logging/transmission software and any dashboard for viewing collected sensor data.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: The actual durability engineering for extreme polar ocean conditions, that's applied marine/materials engineering requiring real research, not assumed specifications.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-suggested durability design without real materials/engineering validation could specify approaches that sound reasonable but wouldn't actually survive genuine Southern Ocean conditions.

data_resource_availability.status: No real long-term extreme-condition test data accessible; a basic working prototype plus researched design proposal is the practical path.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, real field validation is genuinely beyond hackathon scope for this PS.

judge_qna.question: How long would this platform actually survive in real Southern Ocean conditions?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be honest: this hasn't been validated, real long-term survivability testing requires field deployment over months, our contribution is a working measurement prototype and a durability design grounded in real materials/marine-engineering research.
judge_qna.follow_up: What specific durability research did you base your design proposal on?

judge_qna.question: How is this actually lower-cost than existing observation platforms?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific cost breakdown and compare it against known costs of existing platforms, real numbers, not a general 'low-cost' claim.
judge_qna.follow_up: What tradeoff did you make to achieve that cost reduction, and what does it cost you in capability or durability?
